doc.title: Fred Radke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Hillsdale, Michigan, November 8, 2023

title: Jazz Connoisseur and how Harry fired people
summary: Harry called a chart Radke had not played, handed the lead down, and fired by saying go home.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: enforcement — a national law enforcement association or something. And they said, “And now, Harry James” and he walks out and people applaud. Harry comes up and he says — and he always started with the theme, like we do, “Ciribiribin” and then “Don’t Be That Way” because that’s what Benny opened Carnegie Hall with. We still do that. That’s tradition. And it fits. And he walked on the stage and he says, “Jazz Connoisseur.” Well that’s one of his favorite Ernie Wilkins charts, right? I hadn’t played it yet. I’d been on the band a year. And I look at Sonny, I said, “‘Jazz Connoisseur’? What number is that?” And he says, “I don’t know man.” Okay. And then he looked at me and he says, “Fred are you playing lead on this?” And I said, “Yeah.” And he says, Pass it down to the fourth trumpet player.” He’s one of the guys. He did that for about three songs. And then they were gone the next day. And when Harry used to fire people he’d say — not very often — but he’d walk up to you and say, “Go home.”

Not like a “You’re fired, get off my bandstand.” He’d say, “Go home.” And we were on the band bus and Connie Hayes was standing next to me and we were on the Fiftieth Anniversary. And I don’t know, somebody said something. I said, “Why don’t you go home?” And she says, “I haven’t heard that phrase since I was with Harry James in 1939.” I said, “What? Go home?” She says, “Oh yeah, that’s how he used to fire guys.” He’d say, “Go home.” Very low key to get the point across.
